newsitem.title: GERMANY: West losing patience with Bosnia -- Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: West losing patience with Bosnia -- Kinkel.

text.p: Bosnia's conflict parties must work together to forge a lasting peace or face losing the assistance being provided by the West, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Friday,
Kinkel said after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana that both agreed the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) supporting the peace process must be withdrawn as planned next year.

But he said that on a recent trip to Bosnia "I got the abundantly clear impression that the civilian implementation (of the Dayton peace accord) is so far behind that we must be very concerned about the end of the SFOR mandate".
"The parties must know that they not only took on commitments in Dayton but that it is in their own interests to fulfil them," he told reporters.

"While the (three-member) presidium cannot agree on a seating order, while there is no agreement on common car licence plates, while there are no common broadcasting and telephone links -- these are just examples -- the conflict parties cannot expect the international community to maintain its incredible efforts. We cannot serve everything up on a silver platter.
"If the readiness to cooperate is not there, the parties should know that there is also another way of doing things."

Representatives of the five-nation Contact Group on Bosnia met in Brussels on Thursday to prepare for a ministerial-level meeting in Portugal on May 30 of the international steering committee supervising implementation of the Dayton accord.

The Bonn Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the group agreed that "reconstruction aid supplied by the international community will be made strictly dependent on the elimination of failures to implement (the Dayton agreement)."
The Contact Group comprises Russia, the United States, Germany, Britain and France.
